posts.title: World's fastest (panel) QR factorization on B200
posts.description: GPU MODE recently hosted a series of leaderboards for linear algebra kernels . I participated in the first one, QR decomposition, and claimed the 2nd place. I think it’s a breath of fresh air, a departure from the usual LLM-oriented kernels most people program for nowadays. As usual, my submission is open-sourced at gau-nernst/gpu-mode-kernels . The final submission is codex/submission.py . Table

posts.description: Some time ago, I explored using CuteDSL to write some kernels for vLLM to enjoy the JIT benefits (ability to specialize on more parameters, don’t need to recompile vLLM from source during development, etc…). posts.title: tcgen05 for dummies
posts.description: tcgen05 is the set of PTX instructions to program Tensor Cores on the latest NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs ( sm100 , not to be confused with consumer Blackwell sm120 ). At the time of writing, I couldn’t find a Blackwell tutorial in plain CUDA C++ with PTX, even though such exist for Ampere ( alexarmbr’s and spatters’ ) and Hopper ( Pranjal’s ).
